findings.reason: the repo's own rule is to verify an already-correct guard and add the missing test rather than reimplement it, so a node following §2 as written may edit working liveness code instead of establishing why that guard did not fire in the reproduction.
findings.text: §2 states "`local_liveness` is extended for the state the reproduction named, so a run whose worker lives is never classified complete or scoring", but `local_liveness` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:730) already reads the run directory's worker record and returns alive when the supervisor's pointer pid is gone — its own docstring names exactly this case ("a supervisor that exits before its worker takes the pointer pid with it … The worker record is asked next"), and recovery_classification.py:149 already calls it; §2's "What already exists" inventory lists only the precedence test and omits this, so the section reads as though the guard is missing

findings.reason: the count is given as the justification for growing `signal_worker` as the single interface, and that design is unaffected; session_host signals only its own session children, which the node does not touch.
findings.text: §2 asserts "`signal_worker` in `reckon/crew/routing.py` is the only function in the crew that sends a signal", but `session_host.py` sends SIGTERM/SIGKILL through its own `_signal` (reckon/crew/session_host.py:649-653, called at 518/522), an independent signal path in the same package

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited module and symbol resolves (`signal_worker` routing.py:2837, `_process_children`/`_live_descendant` recovery_liveness.py:258/289, `_processes_holding` routing.py:2512, `local_liveness` recovery_liveness.py:730, `terminate` dispatch_sessions.py:1752, all four test files exist); the new test file is correctly absent. No extensionless hrefs. (`STOP_GRACE` is stated where the code defines `STOP_GRACE_ENV`/`STOP_GRACE_DEFAULT`; a reader still finds the grace.)
rubric_items.done_when: pass — s2 and s3 each carry a measurable done-when and each declares a negative control that fails a named case (s2 line 73 signals the supervisor pid alone; s3 line 98 restores the reproduced cause).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — negative-control and gate logs are declared "logged under the run directory" (durable, `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/`), and the tests run in a `$TMPDIR`-scoped temporary tree, not a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach the new symbols or the cited write paths; `§47` appears only as plan prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 commits to *extending* `local_liveness` for the supervisor-exited/worker-alive state, but that state is already the case `local_liveness` exists to cover, so the stated repair targets a guard that is already present.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s2 carries one goal (a run's tree has one live writer: end its process tree and never classify a live worker as done); the process-ending and classification repairs serve that one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` wires `s3 → a-run-has-one-live-writer#s2`, and the new section gate `g-arholw-routing-released` (`data-gated-sections="s2"`) resolves its required evidence to a real anchor, `crew-runtime-positive-controls#s47`; the live run `a-worktree-release-is-whole` it names exists in the live pointer set.
